answer:
Based on published research, the arable sites in Bavaria and Konya can implement several changes to cut fuel. These savings are estimates, not guarantees, and any differences are things to investigate, not proof of a fault or waste. Because these ideas overlap, their savings must not be added together.

Here are the top opportunities:

* **Shift up / throttle down** (Strong evidence): This could save 322 to 1,505 litres (estimated) of fuel per year in Bavaria, and 30 to 140 litres (estimated) in Konya. This is backed by the research sources "Shift Up and Throttle Back to Save Tractor Fuel (PM 2089)", "Analysis of Nebraska tractor test data (MicroCAD 2025)", and "Reduction Rates of Fuel Consumption by Gear Up and Throttle Down on an Agricultural Tractor".
* **Reduced / conservation tillage** (Strong evidence): This could save 304 to 1,506 litres (estimated) of fuel per year in Bavaria, and 34 to 167 litres (estimated) in Konya. This is backed by "Košutić et al. 2007 — conservation tillage (type II) winter wheat", "Conservation tillage vs plough (flow-meter measurement)", and "Reduced tillage vs deep ploughing maize. Energy 69 (2014) 227-235".
* **No-till** (Moderate evidence): This could save 2,240 to 2,912 litres (estimated) of fuel per year in Bavaria, and 187 to 243 litres (estimated) in Konya. This is backed by "Košutić et al. 2007 — no-till winter wheat" and "The Economic Advantages of No-Till: Diesel Fuel (citing Hanna et al. 2001)".
* **Correct tyre pressure** (Moderate evidence): This could save 207 to 1,183 litres (estimated) of fuel per year in Bavaria, and 12 to 69 litres (estimated) in Konya. This is backed by "Tyre pressure and ballast effects on tractor fuel use", "Tuned front/rear tyre pressure", and "Correct tyre pressures save fuel and time (field test 2023)".

As a practical next step, you can check the tyre pressures on the tractors at both sites to begin capturing these savings.

findings.title: The recorder on Tractor 4, 163 kW froze for 92 hours

litres.label: measured
litres.how:
- The recorder on Tractor 4, 163 kW saved **the same readings, over and over, for 92.2 hours**: engine speed, fuel flow and position never changed.
- The frozen stretches fall in these months: **May 2025 (1.7 h), August 2025 (2.0 h), September 2025 (25.9 h), October 2025 (35.1 h), November 2025 (11.1 h), March 2026 (6.5 h), April 2026 (10.1 h)**.

- A working tractor does not do that, so this is a **recording fault**, not real work.
- We **left those hours out** and counted no fuel for them. The fuel burned in that time is unknown, not zero.
- So the fleet's real fuel use may be **higher** than shown. Check this tractor's recorder and its connection.

answer:
No, el combustible de este año no cuadra perfectamente. Se han detectado varias discrepancias importantes que indican que falta combustible en los registros o que se ha registrado de forma incorrecta. Estas diferencias son aspectos a investigar y no constituyen una prueba definitiva de fallos, robos o pérdidas.

Aquí están los hallazgos principales:

* **Falta de stock en el depósito de Arable site (Bavaria)**: Se ha detectado un faltante de aproximadamente 900 litros (measured) en enero de 2026. Los libros indicaban que debería haber 3,255 litros (measured) en el tanque, pero el nivel medido fue de 2,354 litros (measured). Los datos respaldan que el combustible salió del tanque sin un registro de dispensación (un retiro no registrado), ya que la brecha de unos 900 litros (measured) se mantuvo en las lecturas de los meses siguientes.
* **Nota de entrega duplicada en Vineyard site (Tuscany)**: La nota de entrega DN-S2-0004 por 900 litros (measured) se introdujo dos veces en el registro el 8 de septiembre de 2025, lo que hace que los libros muestren 900 litros (measured) de combustible que nunca llegaron.
* **Suministro excesivo en el Tractor 4, 163 kW**: En octubre de 2025, en Arable site (Bavaria), se le suministraron 2,436 litros (measured) de combustible, pero el tractor solo registró un consumo de 2,021 litros (measured), lo que representa 415 litros (measured) más de lo que consumió (un 21% (measured) más). Los datos respaldan que se realizaron 6 suministros nocturnos (measured) que suman 406 litros (measured) fuera de las horas de trabajo (sin tareas registradas en un margen de 2 horas (measured)). Además, el registrador de este tractor se congeló durante 35 horas (measured) en octubre (y un total de 92 horas (measured) en el año), por lo que el consumo real podría ser mayor.

Voici les principales opportunités identifiées pour les sites arables :

* **Shift up / throttle down** (Preuve forte) : Cette méthode permet d'économiser entre 322 litres (estimated) et 1,505 litres (estimated) de carburant par an pour le site **Arable site (Bavaria)**, soit une réduction de coût entre £231 (estimated) et £1,770 (estimated) par an et une réduction d'émissions entre 1.1 tonnes (estimated) et 5.1 tonnes (estimated) de CO2e par an. Cette opportunité est basée sur les recherches *Shift Up and Throttle Back to Save Tractor Fuel (PM 2089)*, *Analysis of Nebraska tractor test data (MicroCAD 2025)* et *Reduction Rates of Fuel Consumption by Gear Up and Throttle Down on an Agricultural Tractor*.
* **Reduced / conservation tillage** (Preuve forte) : Cette méthode permet d'économiser entre 304 litres (estimated) et 1,506 litres (estimated) de carburant par an pour le site **Arable site (Bavaria)**, soit une réduction de coût entre £218 (estimated) et £1,771 (estimated) par an et une réduction d'émissions entre 1.0 tonnes (estimated) et 5.1 tonnes (estimated) de CO2e par an. Cette opportunité est basée sur les recherches *Košutić et al. 2007 — conservation tillage (type II) winter wheat*, *Conservation tillage vs plough (flow-meter measurement)* et *Reduced tillage vs deep ploughing maize. Energy 69 (2014) 227-235*.
* **No-till** (Preuve modérée) : Cette méthode permet d'économiser entre 2,240 litres (estimated) et 2,912 litres (estimated) de carburant par an pour le site **Arable site (Bavaria)**, soit une réduction de coût entre £1,609 (estimated) et £3,425 (estimated) par an et une réduction d'émissions entre 7.6 tonnes (estimated) et 9.8 tonnes (estimated) de CO2e par an. Cette opportunité est basée sur les recherches *Košutić et al. 2007 — no-till winter wheat* et *The Economic Advantages of No-Till: Diesel Fuel (citing Hanna et al. 2001)*.
* **Opportunité pour le site Tillage site (Konya)** : La méthode **Shift up / throttle down** (Preuve forte) permet d'économiser entre 30 litres (estimated) et 140 litres (estimated) de carburant par an pour le site **Tillage site (Konya)**, soit une réduction de coût entre £22 (estimated) et £165 (estimated) par an et une réduction d'émissions entre 0.1 tonnes (estimated) et 0.5 tonnes (estimated) de CO2e par an, selon les recherches *Shift Up and Throttle Back to Save Tractor Fuel (PM 2089)*, *Analysis of Nebraska tractor test data (MicroCAD 2025)* et *Reduction Rates of Fuel Consumption by Gear Up and Throttle Down on an Agricultural Tractor*.

The data supports one main hypothesis for the stock gap at the Arable site (Bavaria) depot, while other possibilities are either unsupported or cannot be tested with our data:

* **Fuel left the tank without a dispense record (unlogged withdrawal)**: This is **supported by the data**. A single unrecorded withdrawal would leave a permanent gap like this. A record of who has the depot key and when the tank was opened would settle this.

* **A delivery was logged but never arrived**: This is **not supported by the data**. There were 0 (measured) logged deliveries to this depot before 31 January 2026 that were entered twice or lacked a paper note.

These findings are things to investigate, not proof of a fault, waste, or loss.
